summary: Amazon installed AI-powered cameras in its delivery vans. Drivers said the cameras wrongly flagged them for unsafe driving, such as when other cars cut them off, which hurt their performance scores and bonuses, with no way to contest the flags.
technical_summary: Netradyne in-cab camera system detects driving 'events' (following distance, stop signs, distraction) and feeds driver scorecards. Misclassification of normal driving, such as mirror checks or being cut off, produced false penalties that affected pay-linked scores, and no appeal mechanism existed.

summary: Buenos Aires used a national fugitive database that includes children to power a live facial recognition system in its subway. The system reportedly led to false arrests, and Human Rights Watch warned it exposed children's data and risked false matches.
technical_summary: A live facial recognition system matches subway camera feeds against headshots linked to CONARC, a national fugitive register. The register is exposed as a plain-text file and includes minors. Matches trigger police alerts and arrests; false matches led to wrongful detentions and no handling protocol existed.
